title: itembank capability support profile
description: One semantic capability's published support profile (Phase 16A, CAP-02, D-16A-2/D-16A-5): the accessible behavior a learner gets, the offline fallback shown when the renderer is not there, the declared renderer availability, the profile version, the concrete check that catches a malformed use, and the capability's real known limits. A profile answers whether a renderer exists and what a learner sees when it does not; it never answers whether a learner may see an answer, a key, a rationale, or a hint tier, which runtime.public_item and runtime.glossable answer and no other module does. offline_fallback carries minLength 1 on purpose: a capability with no declared fallback fails CAP-02's Degraded clause by construction.

name.description: The registry key, unique across the registry; registering a second profile under the same name is refused.

accessible_behavior.description: What a learner using a keyboard, a screen reader, touch, zoom, high contrast, or reduced motion actually gets.

offline_fallback.description: What renders with no network and no scripting. Never empty: a capability with no fallback fails CAP-02's Degraded clause.

renderer_availability.description: The declared ceiling (D-16A-5). A caller's own situation may lower it through capabilities.resolved_availability; nothing may raise it.

version.description: The semantic profile version this capability was described against (D-16A-4).

validation.description: The concrete check that catches a malformed use, named by lint code where one exists. A capability with no validation path says so in plain words.

known_limits.description: A real limitation a reader would actually hit. Never the word none.
